3.0.0.en: Obey not the word: they refuse the good news of Christ.

3.0.1.en: Without the word: by love and good treatment.

3.0.2.en: He asks wives to submit to the leadership of the man, for a woman by her nature inclines to be led by a man whom she trusts, and a man by his nature is suited to lead the woman and care for her. This submission must be in love, so that it wins the hearts of husbands even if they are pagans, as it was at the beginning of Christianity when a pagan wife believed and her husband had not yet believed. Her conduct in the submission of love wins her husband even if she has no opportunity to preach to him in plain words about Christ, for he notices a change in her conduct, namely her submission out of love, and discovers that the secret of this is her faith in Christ.

3.1.0.en: For the sake of the fear of God he asks women to be careful about their conduct and behavior, so that it is not out of fear of her husband or of anyone else but for the sake of God, because fear of people is temporary and is exposed, whereas the fear of God is lasting and gives peace and strength.

3.2.0.en: He forbids them excessive concern for their appearance, and chooses three things from it:

3.2.1.en: 1- Excessive attention to the hair: in the past they used to braid their hair into dozens of plaits.

3.2.2.en: 2- The abundance of jewelry with which they adorn themselves.

3.2.3.en: 3- Luxurious or stumbling clothes, or excessive preoccupation with fashion and attention-grabbing clothing. What is meant is that a woman should be moderate in her adornment and should not let her heart be much occupied with it, because her first concern is God.

3.3.0.en: He directs the woman's attention to care for the inner purity of her heart from all evil and corrupt thoughts, and to being distinguished by inner calm, which also appears in gentle dealings with others; for inner purity and spiritual virtues are the most precious thing before God, who is not concerned with material appearances and outward adornment.

3.4.0.en: He calls the woman to imitate the holy women of the Old Testament, who were obedient to their husbands and concerned with virtues, and who relied on God and not on their beauty and adornment.

3.5.0.en: He gives an example of the holy women of the Old Testament, our mother Sarah, who respected our father Abraham and submitted to him and called him "lord" to show her respect for him. If women feel the motherhood of this saint toward them, as the Jewish men feel the fatherhood of Abraham, then wives should walk like Sarah in being concerned with doing good and relying on God and not on outward adornment. And as God gave Sarah surpassing beauty, He gives wives grace and beauty in the eyes of their husbands.

3.5.1.en: May you be confident that the purity of your heart, your love and your spiritual virtues are stronger than every outward appearance and give you grace in the eyes of God and in the eyes of people.

3.6.0.en: He asks husbands for three things:

3.6.1.en: 1- Wisdom (discernment): in understanding the nature of the woman, which differs from the nature of the man, and taking that into account in dealing with her, such as her distinction in emotion, precision, attention to details, and so on.

3.6.2.en: 2- Not being rough (the feminine vessel as the weaker): taking into account that the woman is weaker in physical strength, so the man does not use his physical strength to achieve his demands or threaten with words of violence and insults.

3.6.3.en: 3- Being occupied with eternity (heirs together of the grace of life): the woman is like the man in her inheritance of the Kingdom, so the man takes into account that the span of life is temporary and is a means of preparation for eternity. He is therefore not preoccupied with fulfilling his material desires, nor does he become angry and furious if they are not fulfilled, because his anger or harshness will make his prayer unacceptable before God, and indeed will make him lose his peace, so that he cannot feel prayer and the comfort in it.

3.6.4.en: May you take into account the natures of others and love them in the way that suits them and not as you yourself see fit, and remember that you will be one with them in the Kingdom around Christ, so that you easily give up the passing matters of this world over which you differ.

3.7.0.en: He asks all the members of the family for the following:

3.7.1.en: 1- Unity of mind: which is achieved through dialogue and understanding and each one's sensitivity to the other, so that they arrive at one feeling and one thought and come out with one opinion, and in this way they overcome all divisions and clashes.

3.7.2.en: 2- Love: offering love by making excuses for those who err, having compassion on the weak, and dealing with gentleness and tenderness in everything.

3.8.0.en: 3- Not resisting evil: no one flares up because of another's anger and returns insulting words or bad deeds; on the contrary, we quench evil with good deeds and words of love and blessing, which declare our good nature as children of God.

3.9.0.en: 4- Good speech: he quotes the words of the Psalm (Ps 34:12-14) to show the importance of keeping away from bad words such as insults or deceit and lying, and rather the Christian expresses himself with good words that show the love that is within him.

3.10.0.en: 5- Peace: if the devil stirs up any problems, they must be stopped, not only by refraining from evil words but also by showing love and doing good with others, so that their agitation calms. Thus the Christian seeks to make peace and sacrifices for it whatever the cost, so he pursues it in his way with all his energy, and God will help him by answering his requests and blessing his life. For whoever sacrifices and endures for the sake of peace is not wronged but is distinguished by God's blessings and fellowship, whereas whoever insists on evil defies God and deserves divine punishment.

3.11.0.en: 7- Reassurance: God's promise to those who do good and make peace, for He grants them inner peace and protects them from evil and does not allow anything to harm them spiritually and hinder the salvation of their souls. Consequently they do not fear people however harsh they may be; on the contrary, God compensates them for their endurance of pain and offence with blessings in their life on earth and in the Kingdom.

3.12.0.en: 8- Inner holiness: God directs the attention of His children to care for consecrating the heart to Him so that they enjoy fellowship with Him, and when they deal with others their faith and their hope in eternity will appear, and their words will be strong and gentle, showing the wicked their weakness and so drawing them to repentance.

3.13.0.en: 9- Purity: care for purity of heart and the rightness of the inner intention, so that your good deeds are linked to a pure heart, and consequently the wicked are put to shame before God for their wickedness and their bad treatment of you, and your endurance of injustice becomes great in God's sight. For whoever suffers for his faults accepts the natural result of his own conduct, but whoever endures offences while his conscience is good and his deeds are good has the divine reward, because it is God who permitted these offences in order to reward His children with inexpressible blessings.

3.13.1.en: Be confident that your endurance of sufferings because of your seeking peace is the conduct of the children of God, and the blessings that await you for your endurance are very many; indeed you are greater than the one who offends you. So do not be shaken however much others cast doubt on you, but have compassion on the offender and pray for him.

3.14.0.en: If the children of God endure sufferings for the sake of doing good and making peace, they are in this following the example of Christ, who suffered, being righteous, for sinners, to save them from eternal death. Having died in the flesh on the cross, He rose on the third day to give life to all who believe in Him, and He makes the endurance of sufferings, with all the troubles that come upon the body and soul, a means for the life and growth of the spirit within everyone who endures. It is a call to bear with sinners and offenders as Christ bore, and He promised spiritual blessings on earth and then in eternal life. Thus sufferings bring us near to God when we endure them: Christ died once on the cross so that we might be put to death for His sake and endure sufferings every day, and so enjoy the life of the Spirit in us.

3.15.2.en: When Christ died on the cross, His soul was separated from His body, but His divinity remained united to both. So Christ went with His divinity united to the human soul to Hades to preach to all the believers of the Old Testament that redemption had been accomplished, in order to bring them up with Him to Paradise.

3.15.3.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic and St. Cyril, the pillar of the faith, say in their interpretation of this verse that with the souls of the saints who were in Hades there were the souls of some people who lived in the days of the Flood and did not believe and enter the ark with Noah, but when the waters rose and they began to drown they repented and declared their faith. Though they were not saved from the Flood with Noah inside the ark, God took account of their faith and their repentance, which came at the end of their life, and when He descended to Hades He saved them with the rest of the believers and brought them up to Paradise. Thus the longsuffering of God appears, and His concern for the salvation of every person who believes, even at the last moment of his life, like the right-hand thief.

3.16.0.en: As God saved Noah and those with him in the ark from the Flood, He saves all of us from eternal death when we die to our sins by being immersed in the water of Baptism. Baptism is not a material washing of the body as human eyes see it, but a new birth and a purification of the heart from every sin, which we receive as a blessing from Christ's redemption of us on the cross.

3.17.0.en: Authorities and powers: ranks of angels.

3.17.1.en: After Christ rose from the dead, He ascended into heaven and sat at the right hand of God, that is, He came into the glory and power that were His from eternity, which He had temporarily set aside before our eyes by appearing in the flesh and enduring sufferings to redeem us. And in His heavenly glory all the angels in their various ranks praise Him and serve Him.

3.17.2.en: God seeks your salvation however far away you are or fallen in sin. Trust in His love and rise quickly to make up for all that is past; He will forgive you everything, and your place in His heart is not shaken, for He has loved you from eternity and awaits your return to Him.

3.17.3.en: Sufferings in the life of the children of God

4.0.s.en: (1) Sufferings and judgment lead to repentance

4.0.1.en: Christians face troubles not only in controlling their lusts but in enduring the mockery of the wicked who used to share their lusts with them. Therefore the Apostle Peter encourages them that Christ endured many sufferings for our redemption, so we follow His example, knowing that any sufferings we bear make us stop and grow weary of sin, for sufferings encourage us to repent.

4.1.0.en: The Christian feels that life is limited, so repentance drives him to leave the lusts of the wicked and to be concerned with carrying out God's commandments and will.

4.2.0.en: The Apostle Peter alerts us to the waste of our past life in various sins; what has happened is enough, so let us now try to use our life for living with God. He lists a group of evident sins in which believers formerly shared with the pagans, which are:

4.2.1.en: Lasciviousness: debauchery and excess in fornication.

4.2.2.en: Lusts: impurity, or the love of foods and possessions...

4.2.3.en: Excess of wine: that is, continuing in drunkenness.

4.2.5.en: Banquetings: sitting with the wicked and taking part in their deeds.

4.2.6.en: Abominable idolatries: with all the accompanying evil lusts that they include.

4.3.0.en: The wicked are surprised at the believers because they have repented of the lusts that they used to practice with them, and also of the rush and persistence in every form of debauchery, which drives these wicked people to abuse the believers and accuse them of sins they did not commit.

4.4.0.en: The Apostle makes clear that the wicked Gentiles will be called to account for all their evil deeds on the Day of Judgment. He says this to establish the believers in repentance and in rejecting evil lusts.

4.5.0.en: For this cause: for the sake of the great Day of Judgment, on which God will call man to account for all the evil he has done.

4.5.1.en: The dead: those who believed in Christ and then died.

4.5.2.en: Be judged according to men: the wicked judge them and persecute them to death.

4.5.3.en: That they might live according to God: life after death in the Paradise of bliss and then the Kingdom of Heaven. So that people would not be condemned on the Day of Judgment, the Apostles preached everywhere, and many believed and endured sufferings from the wicked until they were martyred, and this is the judgment of men that comes upon the flesh only. But these dead believers live in the Spirit with God in the Paradise of bliss.

4.5.4.en: Do not be distressed when some sufferings come upon you, but make them a reason to remember your sins and repent of them, knowing that our life on earth is short, so that you hasten to seize opportunities and draw near to God.

4.6.0.en: When we remember the end of our life and the Day of Judgment we become spiritually vigilant, and this is sobriety, so we pay attention and take care with our prayers, which bring us near to God and are also our whole life in heaven; that is, through prayers we prepare for our eternal life.

4.7.0.en: When we love God through many prayers, a feeling of love for others grows in us, so we are concerned to serve them, and if we see their sins we do not judge them but cover them.

4.8.0.en: Love of the brethren results in the care to show hospitality to strangers, and we do not do it as a heavy duty and so murmur about it, but with love and joy, because by this we receive Christ, as Abraham received strangers and discovered that he had received God and the angels (Gen 18).

4.9.0.en: If one of the believers is distinguished by a gift, such as preaching or the ability to provide for the needs of the needy, he is not proud, but feels that this gift is a grace from God and that he is a steward of it, to use it in the service of the Church.

4.10.0.en: Because gifts are from God, the preacher must speak the words of the Holy Bible and the mind of the Church and not his personal ideas. And whoever performs any service should rely on prayer to receive God's power from it, and servants should glorify God and thank Him before and after their service, because He is the One who acts in the service.

4.10.1.en: Your love for people reveals the measure of your love for God, for love is your only work in the world. Take care to cover people's sins, make excuses for them and help them with all your strength, because your abilities are a gift from God that increases in proportion to how much you use it in caring for others.

4.11.s.en: (3) The reward of those who suffer

4.11.0.en: The Apostle reassures the believers in the midst of the sufferings that meet them from those who persecute them. Even if the persecutions appear like a fiery trial that burns and destroys many aspects of their life, they should not be troubled, because this is to be expected from the evil world that persecutes the children of God.

4.12.0.en: He gives them the good news that, as they have shared in enduring sufferings and persecutions for the sake of Christ, they will share in His eternal glories, and thinking about these glories gives them joy in the midst of their sufferings.

4.13.0.en: He continues his encouragement of the persecuted believers: the insults to which they are exposed make them worthy to receive a greater grace from the Holy Spirit, who comforts them and makes them feel His presence with them and also promises them heavenly glories. Thus, even if the insults appear as blasphemy against Christ on the part of the wicked, they are counted as glory and a crown of blessing for the suffering believers, for Christ is glorified because of their endurance of these sufferings for His sake.

4.14.0.en: He forbids believers to suffer because of their sins, because they must walk in righteousness and keep away from evident sins such as murder or theft or any evil deeds that society rejects and punishes, even small sins such as meddling in the private affairs of others, which troubles them and rouses them against us. The personal freedom of every person must be respected, because these are the sufferings to which the wicked are exposed because of their evils, and they are rejected by God and are not counted as being for the sake of God.

4.15.0.en: But if the believer suffers because he is a Christian and walks in the commandments of God, these sufferings are counted as being for the sake of God, and He supports him in them and rewards him for them.

4.16.0.en: The Apostle encourages us to hold to a life of righteousness and to reject sins by remembering the justice of God, who punishes the wicked, and His discipline will begin with His Jewish people by the destruction of the temple of God in Jerusalem, which Christ foretold to them (Mt 23:38). If God begins by disciplining His children the Jews for their unbelief in Christ, how great will be His discipline and punishment of the wicked pagans who refuse to believe in Him and persist in their sins.

4.17.0.en: He continues to remind them of the justice of God, which requires that righteous believers strive by the grace of their God until He saves them. And naturally the wicked and the ungodly will have no place in the Kingdom, but eternal torment awaits them. This shows the same meaning as is found in (Prov 11:31).

4.18.0.en: At the end of his encouragement of the believers who suffer because of their faith, he calls them to rely on God the Maker of good things, who does not forget their love and endurance and rewards them with heavenly glories.

4.18.1.en: When afflictions and sufferings befall you without your having sinned, accept them from God, confident of His appreciation of your endurance and looking to the eternal reward, and do not offend those who offend you but pray for them. Advice for priests and young people
